findings.title: Blocked-email lookup can be bypassed by changing letter case
findings.body: should_block? performs an exact, case-sensitive database lookup for the supplied email, and neither BlockedEmail nor User normalizes email addresses to lowercase before saving or validation. An address stored as blocked@example.com therefore will not match a signup attempt using Blocked@Example.com or BLOCKED@example.com, allowing a trivial bypass of the block list (PostgreSQL string equality and the unique index are case-sensitive). Normalize addresses (downcase/strip) on both BlockedEmail save and lookup, or use a case-insensitive comparison.

findings.title: should_block? uses a non-atomic read-modify-write inside a validator
findings.body: should_block? increments match_count with `record.match_count += 1` followed by `save`. It is called from EmailValidator during ordinary model validation, so a single signup attempt that calls user.valid? and then user.save runs it at least twice and double-counts one attempt, and two concurrent attempts can read the same match_count and overwrite each other, losing counts. The write also makes validation itself have a database side effect that can fail or participate unexpectedly in surrounding transactions. Use an atomic SQL increment (e.g. update_counters/increment_counter with update for last_match_at) and ideally move the stat update out of the pure predicate/validator path so one rejected attempt is counted once.

findings.title: rejectedEmails is a shared prototype array that is never cleared
findings.body: rejectedEmails is defined as Em.A([]) directly on the controller class prototype, so the same mutable array is shared by controller instances, and createAccount only ever pushObject()s into it. Once an email is rejected it stays rejected for the life of the page session even if the server-side reason disappears (address unblocked, conflicting account removed, admin fixes the record), forcing a page reload before the user can retry that address. Initialize the array per controller instance and clear it when the modal/account flow is reset.
